summary.en-US: A companion for reading W3C specifications and finding the groups and people behind them.

description.en-US:
W3C Companion shows what W3C knows about the page you’re on.

On a W3C or WHATWG specification, it shows the spec’s maturity, its editor’s draft and TR versions, its repository and issue tracker, its tests, and the group responsible for it — with the group’s chairs, team contacts, and charter end date. It tells you when you’re reading a dated snapshot or an old level, shows how many other specifications use each definition, sums up the spec’s place in the web platform, and checks its links to other specs for anchors that no longer exist.

On a W3C repository on GitHub, it shows the group behind the repository and the specs it hosts. On a w3.org group page, it shows the group’s specs.

Type “w3c” and a space in the address bar to search specs, groups, Web IDL names, and terms.

During TPAC 2026 (Dublin, 26–30 October), it shows what’s in session now and next, and when each group meets.

Data comes from public W3C sources: browser-specs, w3c/groups, webref, the W3C API, and the TPAC calendar.

version.approval_notes: The attached source zip builds this version with Node 24 or later: npm ci && npm run build, which writes dist/. The scripts in dist/ are esbuild bundles of src/, unminified, and the JSON files in dist/data/ are snapshots of public W3C data that npm run snapshot regenerates. Source: https://github.com/w3c-oss/w3c-companion
